title: Generative AI for Computer Vision - Full Combined Grand Test (Weeks 1-12)
subject: Generative AI for Computer Vision

questions.question: 1. Which of the following is a generative model?
questions.correctAnswer: GAN
questions.explanation: GAN (Generative Adversarial Network) is a generative model designed to synthesize new data samples that resemble the training distribution, unlike discriminative architectures such as ResNet, U-Net, and AlexNet.

questions.question: 2. The main purpose of a generative vision model is to:
questions.correctAnswer: Generate new images
questions.explanation: The primary purpose of a generative vision model is to learn the underlying probability distribution of images and generate new, unseen visual samples.

questions.question: 3. Which of the following is an application of generative models in computer vision?
questions.correctAnswer: All of the above
questions.explanation: Generative models in computer vision are used for image synthesis, image restoration (super-resolution, inpainting, denoising), and synthetic data augmentation.

questions.question: 4. A joint probability distribution describes:
options: The probability of a single random variable
The probability of two or more random variables occurring together
questions.correctAnswer: The probability of two or more random variables occurring together
questions.explanation: A joint probability distribution represents the probability that two or more random variables simultaneously take on specific values.

questions.question: 5. Correlation measures:
options: The strength and direction of the relationship between two variables
The average value of a variable
The maximum value in a dataset
questions.correctAnswer: The strength and direction of the relationship between two variables
questions.explanation: Correlation measures both the strength and the direction of the linear relationship between two variables.

questions.question: 6. Covariance tells us:
questions.correctAnswer: Whether two variables change together
questions.explanation: Covariance indicates the directional relationship between two variables—showing whether higher values of one variable correspond to higher (or lower) values of another.

questions.question: 7. The objective of Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) is to:
options: Find parameter values that make the observed data most likely
questions.correctAnswer: Find parameter values that make the observed data most likely
questions.explanation: The objective of Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) is to find the model parameters that maximize the likelihood of the observed training dataset.

questions.question: 8. Bayesian learning combines:
questions.correctAnswer: Prior knowledge and observed data
questions.explanation: Bayesian learning uses Bayes' theorem to combine prior knowledge (prior distribution) and observed evidence/data to compute the posterior distribution.

questions.question: 9. Bayesian learning updates model parameters as new evidence becomes available.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In Bayesian inference, prior distributions are iteratively updated to posterior distributions as new empirical data or evidence becomes available.

questions.question: 10. Generative AI models can create new images that resemble the training data.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Generative AI models learn the statistical distribution of training images to synthesize novel images that closely resemble the training dataset.

questions.question: 11. The basic computational unit of an artificial neural network is called:
questions.correctAnswer: Neuron
questions.explanation: An artificial neuron (or node/perceptron) is the fundamental computational unit of an artificial neural network.

questions.question: 12. Which of the following is an application of neural networks?
questions.correctAnswer: All of the above
questions.explanation: Neural networks are widely applied in computer vision (image recognition), audio processing (speech recognition), and natural language processing (NLP).

questions.question: 13. A Single Layer Perceptron (SLP) can correctly solve:
questions.correctAnswer: Linearly separable problems
questions.explanation: A Single Layer Perceptron creates a single linear decision boundary and can only separate classes that are linearly separable.

questions.question: 14. Which of the following is a major limitation of a Single Layer Perceptron?
options: It cannot solve linearly separable problems
It cannot solve non-linearly separable problems such as XOR
It always requires multiple hidden layers
questions.correctAnswer: It cannot solve non-linearly separable problems such as XOR
questions.explanation: A major limitation of a Single Layer Perceptron is that it cannot solve non-linearly separable problems like the XOR function without hidden layers.

questions.question: 15. What is the main purpose of an activation function in a neural network?
options: To introduce non-linearity into the network
To increase the number of input features
questions.correctAnswer: To introduce non-linearity into the network
questions.explanation: Activation functions introduce non-linearities into neural networks, enabling them to learn complex, non-linear relationships rather than just linear combinations.

questions.question: 16. The Softmax activation function is commonly used in the output layer for:
questions.correctAnswer: Multi-class classification
questions.explanation: The Softmax activation function converts raw output logits into a probability distribution summing to 1, making it ideal for multi-class classification.

questions.question: 17. During the forward pass of a neural network:
options: Data moves from the input layer toward the output layer
Data moves only from the output layer to the input layer
Weights are always set to zero
questions.correctAnswer: Data moves from the input layer toward the output layer
questions.explanation: During the forward pass, input data propagates forward through successive layers (calculating weighted sums and activations) to generate predictions at the output layer.

questions.question: 18. What is the main purpose of backpropagation during neural network training?
options: To calculate gradients and help update the network weights
To increase the number of classes
questions.correctAnswer: To calculate gradients and help update the network weights
questions.explanation: Backpropagation computes the gradients of the loss function with respect to the network weights via the chain rule, enabling optimization algorithms (like SGD) to update the weights.

questions.question: 19. Overfitting occurs when:
options: A model performs well on training data but poorly on unseen data
A model performs equally well on all datasets
A model has no trainable parameters
questions.correctAnswer: A model performs well on training data but poorly on unseen data
questions.explanation: Overfitting happens when a model memorizes patterns and noise specific to the training set, causing it to generalize poorly to unseen validation or test data.

questions.question: 20. Which of the following techniques can help reduce overfitting?
questions.correctAnswer: All of the above
questions.explanation: Techniques such as weight regularization (L1/L2), dropout, early stopping, and cross-validation are standard methods to mitigate overfitting.

questions.question: 21. CNN stands for:
questions.correctAnswer: Convolutional Neural Network
questions.explanation: CNN stands for Convolutional Neural Network, a deep learning architecture specialized for grid-structured data such as images.

questions.question: 22. Each neuron in a convolutional layer is connected only to:
options: a small local region (patch) of the input image
questions.correctAnswer: a small local region (patch) of the input image
questions.explanation: Each neuron in a convolutional layer is connected only to a small local region (patch) of the input instead of the entire input image, defined by its receptive field.

questions.question: 23. What is the primary purpose of the convolution layer in a CNN?
options: Extract features from the input image
questions.correctAnswer: Extract features from the input image
questions.explanation: Convolution layers apply learnable filters to extract visual features such as edges, textures, and higher-level patterns from the input image.

questions.question: 24. Pooling is mainly used to:
options: Reduce the spatial dimensions of feature maps
questions.correctAnswer: Reduce the spatial dimensions of feature maps
questions.explanation: Pooling reduces the spatial dimensions (height and width) of feature maps, which reduces computation and parameters while providing translation invariance.

questions.question: 25. Which of the following is a famous CNN architecture?
questions.correctAnswer: AlexNet
questions.explanation: AlexNet is a landmark CNN architecture designed by Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, and Geoffrey Hinton that won the ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge in 2012.

questions.question: 26. Which CNN architecture introduced the Inception module?
questions.correctAnswer: GoogLeNet
questions.explanation: GoogLeNet (Inception v1) introduced the Inception module to perform convolutions at multiple scales (1x1, 3x3, 5x5) and pooling in parallel within the same layer.

questions.question: 27. GoogLeNet is known for using:
questions.correctAnswer: Inception Module
questions.explanation: GoogLeNet is famous for its Inception module, which combines multiple parallel convolution operations (including 1×1, 3×3, and 5×5 filters) to capture multi-scale features efficiently.

questions.question: 28. Which problem commonly occurs when very deep neural networks are trained?
questions.correctAnswer: Vanishing gradient problem
questions.explanation: In very deep networks, backpropagated gradients can shrink exponentially through many layers, causing earlier layers to learn very slowly or stall completely (vanishing gradient problem).

questions.question: 29. Which activation function helps reduce the vanishing gradient problem?
questions.correctAnswer: ReLU
questions.explanation: ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit) has a constant gradient of 1 for all positive inputs, avoiding gradient saturation and mitigating the vanishing gradient problem in deep networks.

questions.question: 30. True/False? Increasing the number of layers always improves the performance of a neural network.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Simply making a network deeper does not always improve performance because deep networks can suffer from vanishing/exploding gradients, optimization degradation, and overfitting.

questions.question: 31. What is the main idea behind ResNet?
questions.correctAnswer: To use residual (skip) connections
questions.explanation: ResNet introduces residual (skip) connections that allow information to bypass intermediate layers, enabling the training of networks with hundreds of layers.

questions.question: 32. A skip (residual) connection allows information to:
questions.correctAnswer: Skip one or more layers
questions.explanation: A skip connection directly forwards the input of a layer/block to its output by identity mapping, skipping one or more intermediate transformation layers.

questions.question: 33. What is the main advantage of skip connections?
options: They reduce the number of classes.
They help reduce the vanishing gradient problem.
questions.correctAnswer: They help reduce the vanishing gradient problem.
questions.explanation: Skip connections provide a direct highway for gradients to flow backwards during backpropagation, effectively preventing the vanishing gradient problem.

questions.question: 34. DenseNet differs from ResNet because:
options: Each layer is connected to every previous layer.
It uses only fully connected layers.
questions.correctAnswer: Each layer is connected to every previous layer.
questions.explanation: In DenseNet (Densely Connected Convolutional Networks), each layer receives feature maps concatenated from all preceding layers, maximizing feature reuse and gradient flow.

questions.question: 35. Which CNN architecture is specifically designed for handheld and embedded devices?
questions.correctAnswer: MobileNet
questions.explanation: MobileNet uses depthwise separable convolutions to dramatically reduce parameter count and computational complexity, making it ideal for mobile and embedded devices.

questions.question: 36. EfficientNet mainly improves performance by:
options: Scaling network depth, width, and resolution synchronously
questions.correctAnswer: Scaling network depth, width, and resolution synchronously
questions.explanation: EfficientNet introduces compound scaling, uniformly scaling network depth, width, and image resolution with a fixed compound coefficient for optimal accuracy and efficiency.

questions.question: 37. Sequence modeling is mainly used for:
questions.correctAnswer: Processing sequential data
questions.explanation: Sequence modeling deals with sequential, time-dependent data where the order of elements carries semantic meaning, such as text, speech, and time-series.

questions.question: 38. RNN stands for:
questions.correctAnswer: Recurrent Neural Network
questions.explanation: RNN stands for Recurrent Neural Network, an architecture designed to process sequential data by maintaining an internal recurrent state.

questions.question: 39. Which of the following is a common application of RNN?
questions.correctAnswer: Language translation
questions.explanation: RNNs and recurrent sequence-to-sequence models are widely used for sequential applications such as machine translation, speech recognition, and language modeling.

questions.question: 40. The main feature of an RNN is that it:
options: Uses temporal context while processing sequences
questions.correctAnswer: Uses temporal context while processing sequences
questions.explanation: RNNs maintain a recurring hidden state that preserves historical context across time steps, allowing the model to use temporal context while processing sequences.

questions.question: 41. What is the main purpose of Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT) in an RNN?
options: To train the RNN by computing gradients over time
questions.correctAnswer: To train the RNN by computing gradients over time
questions.explanation: BPTT unrolls the RNN across the sequence time steps and propagates gradients backward through time to update network parameters.

questions.question: 42. In a character-level RNN, the model processes:
questions.correctAnswer: Individual characters in a sequence
questions.explanation: In character-level modeling, the RNN processes one character at each time step, learning vocabulary structure, spelling, and character transitions.

questions.question: 43. Which problem is commonly associated with traditional RNNs?
questions.correctAnswer: Vanishing gradient problem
questions.explanation: In standard RNNs, gradients propagated over many time steps undergo repeated matrix multiplications, often shrinking exponentially (vanishing gradients) and hindering long-term dependency learning.

questions.question: 44. Which neural network architecture is specifically designed to handle long-term dependencies in sequential data?
questions.correctAnswer: LSTM
questions.explanation: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks incorporate gating mechanisms (forget, input, and output gates) and a cell state to regulate information flow and preserve long-term dependencies.

questions.question: 45. What is the main purpose of the attention mechanism in sequence-to-sequence models?
options: To reduce the number of classes
To focus on the most relevant parts of the input sequence
questions.correctAnswer: To focus on the most relevant parts of the input sequence
questions.explanation: The attention mechanism enables the decoder to dynamically attend to and weigh the most relevant parts of the input sequence for each output token.

questions.question: 46. Computer vision mainly deals with:
options: Understanding and analyzing images and videos
questions.correctAnswer: Understanding and analyzing images and videos
questions.explanation: Computer vision is an interdisciplinary field of AI enabling computational systems to process, analyze, and interpret visual data from the real world.

questions.question: 47. Which of the following is a common computer vision task?
questions.correctAnswer: All of the above
questions.explanation: Image classification (labeling an image), object detection (localizing and categorizing objects with bounding boxes), and semantic segmentation (pixel-level labeling) are core tasks in computer vision.

questions.question: 48. What is image super-resolution used for?
options: Increasing the resolution or quality of an image
questions.correctAnswer: Increasing the resolution or quality of an image
questions.explanation: Image super-resolution reconstructs a high-resolution, sharp image from one or more degraded low-resolution input images.

questions.question: 49. Which of the following is an application of Generative AI in computer vision?
questions.correctAnswer: All of the above
questions.explanation: Generative AI powers numerous computer vision applications including style transfer/image translation (e.g., Pix2Pix, CycleGAN), synthetic medical imaging, and photorealistic face generation.

questions.question: 50. What is image in-painting?
options: Converting an image into a table
Reducing the number of image classes
Filling or reconstructing missing regions of an image
Removing all colors from an image
questions.correctAnswer: Filling or reconstructing missing regions of an image
questions.explanation: Image inpainting is the process of restoring or reconstructing missing, deteriorated, or intentionally masked parts of an image using context from surrounding regions.

questions.question: 51. What is the main goal of a generative model?
options: To generate new data similar to the training data
To reduce the number of classes
questions.correctAnswer: To generate new data similar to the training data
questions.explanation: Generative models learn the underlying true data distribution p(x) in order to sample and generate new data instances that closely resemble the training distribution.

questions.question: 52. What does Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) try to find?
options: Parameters that make the observed data most likely
questions.correctAnswer: Parameters that make the observed data most likely
questions.explanation: Maximum Likelihood Estimation estimates model parameters by selecting values that maximize the probability (likelihood) of observing the given dataset.

questions.question: 53. What is density estimation used for?
options: Estimating the probability distribution of data
questions.correctAnswer: Estimating the probability distribution of data
questions.explanation: Density estimation involves constructing an estimate of an unobservable underlying probability density function based on observed data.

questions.question: 54. What is an autoregressive model?
options: A model that predicts the current value using previous values
A model that only processes images
A model that does not use previous information
A model used only for data compression
questions.correctAnswer: A model that predicts the current value using previous values
questions.explanation: An autoregressive model uses the chain rule of probability to predict each subsequent variable conditioned on all previously generated/observed values.

questions.question: 55. PixelCNN is mainly used for:
questions.correctAnswer: Generating images pixel by pixel
questions.explanation: PixelCNN is a generative autoregressive neural network that generates images sequentially pixel by pixel using masked convolutions to model dependencies.

questions.question: 56. In PixelRNN, the name "RNN" refers to:
questions.correctAnswer: Recurrent Neural Network
questions.explanation: PixelRNN uses recurrent neural networks (such as Diagonal BiLSTM or Row LSTM) to model sequential pixel dependencies during image generation.

questions.question: 57. What does spatial context in an image refer to?
options: Information about the relationships between nearby or different regions in an image
questions.correctAnswer: Information about the relationships between nearby or different regions in an image
questions.explanation: Spatial context captures geometric and positional relationships between adjacent pixels, visual patches, or semantic entities across an image.

questions.question: 58. Image captioning aims to:
options: Generate a textual description of an image
questions.correctAnswer: Generate a textual description of an image
questions.explanation: Image captioning bridges computer vision and natural language processing to produce natural language descriptions describing the contents of an image.

questions.question: 59. What is the main purpose of attention in image captioning?
options: To reduce the image file size
To focus on relevant parts of an image while generating a caption
questions.correctAnswer: To focus on relevant parts of an image while generating a caption
questions.explanation: Attention mechanisms allow an image captioning model to dynamically focus on relevant spatial regions of the image corresponding to each generated word.

questions.question: 60. A Fully Visible Belief Network (FVBN) is a type of:
questions.correctAnswer: Generative model
questions.explanation: A Fully Visible Belief Network (FVBN) is an autoregressive generative model where all variables are observed and their joint distribution is factorized via conditional probabilities.

questions.question: 61. What is the main purpose of the attention mechanism?
options: To focus on the most relevant parts of the input
To reduce the number of classes
questions.correctAnswer: To focus on the most relevant parts of the input
questions.explanation: The attention mechanism enables neural networks to compute dynamic importance weights and focus selectively on the most relevant components of the input.

questions.question: 62. In self-attention, the model mainly relates:
options: Only the first and last elements
Only the input and output images
Different parts of the same input sequence
questions.correctAnswer: Different parts of the same input sequence
questions.explanation: Self-attention (intra-attention) relates different positions within the same input sequence to compute a contextualized representation of that sequence.

questions.question: 63. What is the purpose of masked self-attention?
options: To prevent a position from attending to future positions
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent a position from attending to future positions
questions.explanation: Masked self-attention applies an upper-triangular mask (setting future positions to negative infinity) to prevent autoregressive models from attending to subsequent tokens during generation.

questions.question: 64. Multi-head self-attention uses:
options: Multiple attention heads to capture different relationships
questions.correctAnswer: Multiple attention heads to capture different relationships
questions.explanation: Multi-head attention projects queries, keys, and values into multiple representation subspaces, allowing the model to jointly attend to different types of contextual relationships.

questions.question: 65. A Transformer is mainly based on:
questions.correctAnswer: Attention mechanisms
questions.explanation: Transformers rely entirely on self-attention and cross-attention mechanisms to model relationships between input elements, eliminating recurrence and convolutions.

questions.question: 66. How does a Vision Transformer (ViT) process an image?
options: It converts the image directly into audio
It divides the image into patches and processes them as tokens
questions.correctAnswer: It divides the image into patches and processes them as tokens
questions.explanation: Vision Transformers divide an image into fixed-size non-overlapping patches (e.g., 16×16), linearly project them into patch embeddings, prepend a class token, add positional embeddings, and feed them into a standard Transformer encoder.

questions.question: 67. One major difference between a Transformer and a CNN is that:
options: Transformers use attention to model relationships between input elements
CNNs do not have trainable parameters
questions.correctAnswer: Transformers use attention to model relationships between input elements
questions.explanation: Unlike CNNs that rely on localized convolution kernels with fixed receptive fields, Transformers use self-attention to model global dependencies directly across all input elements.

questions.question: 68. What is the main role of the Transformer encoder?
options: To transform the input into useful contextual representations
questions.correctAnswer: To transform the input into useful contextual representations
questions.explanation: The Transformer encoder processes the input embeddings through multi-head self-attention and feed-forward sublayers to generate rich, contextualized representations.

questions.question: 69. What is the purpose of input embedding?
options: To convert input tokens into numerical vector representations
To increase the number of images
questions.correctAnswer: To convert input tokens into numerical vector representations
questions.explanation: Input embedding maps discrete input tokens (such as word tokens or flattened image patches) into continuous dense vector representations suitable for neural network processing.

questions.question: 70. Why is positional encoding used in a Transformer?
options: To provide information about the position or order of input elements
To reduce the number of attention heads
questions.correctAnswer: To provide information about the position or order of input elements
questions.explanation: Because self-attention is permutation-invariant and lacks inherent recurrence or convolution, positional encodings are injected into the input embeddings to provide information about the sequential ordering of elements.

questions.question: 71. What is the main idea of a Vision Transformer (ViT)?
options: To process images using image patches as tokens
questions.correctAnswer: To process images using image patches as tokens
questions.explanation: Vision Transformer divides an image into smaller patches and treats these patches as tokens that can be processed using Transformer mechanisms.

questions.question: 72. DETR stands for:
questions.correctAnswer: Detection Transformer
questions.explanation: DETR stands for DEtection TRansformer and uses a Transformer-based architecture for object detection.

questions.question: 73. What is a key feature of the Swin Transformer?
options: It uses shifted windows for self-attention
It uses only fully connected layers
questions.correctAnswer: It uses shifted windows for self-attention
questions.explanation: Swin Transformer uses local windows for self-attention and shifts these windows between layers to allow information exchange between neighboring windows.

questions.question: 74. What is the main purpose of an Auto-Encoder?
options: To increase the number of input features
To learn a compact representation of the input data
questions.correctAnswer: To learn a compact representation of the input data
questions.explanation: An Auto-Encoder learns to encode input data into a compact representation and then reconstruct the original input.

questions.question: 75. An Auto-Encoder mainly consists of:
questions.correctAnswer: Encoder and Decoder
questions.explanation: An Auto-Encoder has two main parts: the encoder, which creates a compact representation, and the decoder, which reconstructs the input.

questions.question: 76. Which of the following is a difference between a Variational Auto-Encoder (VAE) and a traditional Auto-Encoder?
options: VAE does not have an encoder
VAE does not have a decoder
VAE learns a probability distribution for the latent representation
questions.correctAnswer: VAE learns a probability distribution for the latent representation
questions.explanation: A VAE learns a probability distribution over the latent space, allowing it to sample new latent representations and generate new data.

questions.question: 77. In a VAE, the typical sequence of operations is:
questions.correctAnswer: Encoding → Sampling → Decoding
questions.explanation: In a VAE, the input is first encoded into parameters of a latent distribution, a latent vector is sampled, and the decoder uses that sample to reconstruct or generate data.

questions.question: 78. In a VAE, the latent variable is generally:
options: A sampled representation of the input
questions.correctAnswer: A sampled representation of the input
questions.explanation: The latent variable is sampled from the distribution learned by the encoder and is used by the decoder to reconstruct or generate data.

questions.question: 79. In a VAE, why is sampling performed in the latent space?
options: To enable generation of different possible outputs
questions.correctAnswer: To enable generation of different possible outputs
questions.explanation: Sampling allows a VAE to generate different data samples from its learned latent distribution.

questions.question: 80. What is the main purpose of the problem formulation in a VAE?
options: To increase the number of images
To define how the input data and its underlying probability distribution are modelled
To replace the decoder with a CNN
questions.correctAnswer: To define how the input data and its underlying probability distribution are modelled
questions.explanation: The problem formulation specifies how the observed data is related to latent variables and how the model can learn a useful probability distribution for generating data.

questions.question: 81. What is the main purpose of a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)?
options: To generate new data similar to the training data
questions.correctAnswer: To generate new data similar to the training data
questions.explanation: The main purpose of a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) is to generate new, synthetic data samples that closely mimic the distribution of the training data.

questions.question: 82. A GAN mainly consists of which two networks?
questions.correctAnswer: Generator and Discriminator
questions.explanation: A GAN consists of two competing neural networks: a Generator that creates synthetic data samples and a Discriminator that distinguishes between real and generated samples.

questions.question: 83. What is the main role of the Generator in a GAN?
options: To distinguish real and fake data
To remove noise from the dataset
questions.correctAnswer: To generate fake data samples
questions.explanation: The Generator takes random noise as input and maps it to realistic synthetic data samples aimed at deceiving the Discriminator.

questions.question: 84. What is a common problem when training GANs?
questions.correctAnswer: Mode collapse
questions.explanation: Mode collapse is a classic failure mode during GAN training where the Generator produces only a limited variety of outputs, repeatedly generating the same or similar samples.

questions.question: 85. What is the main idea of a Conditional GAN (cGAN)?
options: It generates data based on additional information such as class labels
It does not use a Discriminator
It can only generate random noise
questions.correctAnswer: It generates data based on additional information such as class labels
questions.explanation: Conditional GANs (cGANs) condition both the Generator and Discriminator on additional auxiliary information (such as class labels or text) to control the generation process.

questions.question: 86. What is the main purpose of Wasserstein GAN (WGAN)?
options: To improve the stability of GAN training
questions.correctAnswer: To improve the stability of GAN training
questions.explanation: Wasserstein GAN utilizes the Earth Mover's (Wasserstein-1) Distance to provide smooth, meaningful gradients everywhere, significantly improving training stability and alleviating mode collapse.

questions.question: 87. What happens during the forward diffusion process in a diffusion model?
options: The model directly generates the final image
Noise is completely removed from the data
Noise is gradually added to the data
questions.correctAnswer: Noise is gradually added to the data
questions.explanation: In the forward diffusion process, Gaussian noise is gradually added to an image across discrete time steps until it becomes pure random noise.

questions.question: 88. What happens during reverse diffusion?
options: Noise is gradually removed to generate data
questions.correctAnswer: Noise is gradually removed to generate data
questions.explanation: In reverse diffusion, a trained neural network iteratively predicts and removes noise from a random Gaussian sample to synthesize a clean, high-quality image.

questions.question: 89. What is the full form of DDPM?
questions.correctAnswer: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model
questions.explanation: DDPM stands for Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model, a foundational class of generative models introduced by Ho et al. (2020).

questions.question: 90. What is the main purpose of the ELBO in a VAE or diffusion-model formulation?
options: To provide an objective for learning the generative model
questions.correctAnswer: To provide an objective for learning the generative model
questions.explanation: The Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO) provides a mathematically tractable surrogate objective function to maximize the log-likelihood of observed data in latent variable models.

questions.question: 91. What is the main purpose of a Large Language Model (LLM)?
options: To understand and generate human-like text
To remove all text from a dataset
questions.correctAnswer: To understand and generate human-like text
questions.explanation: An LLM is trained to process and generate text by learning patterns and relationships in large amounts of language data.

questions.question: 92. Which architecture is commonly used to build modern Large Language Models?
questions.correctAnswer: Transformer
questions.explanation: Modern LLMs commonly use the Transformer architecture because it can efficiently model relationships between tokens in a sequence.

questions.question: 93. What is the purpose of tokenization in an LLM?
options: To convert text into smaller units that the model can process
To convert text directly into images
questions.correctAnswer: To convert text into smaller units that the model can process
questions.explanation: Tokenization converts text into tokens, such as words, subwords, or characters, which can then be converted into numerical representations for the model.

questions.question: 94. What is the main purpose of pre-training an LLM?
options: To train only on one image
To learn general patterns from a large amount of text data
questions.correctAnswer: To learn general patterns from a large amount of text data
questions.explanation: During pre-training, an LLM learns general language patterns, relationships, and knowledge from a large collection of text data.

questions.question: 95. What is fine-tuning in an LLM?
options: Further training a pre-trained model for a specific task or domain
questions.correctAnswer: Further training a pre-trained model for a specific task or domain
questions.explanation: Fine-tuning adapts a pre-trained model to perform better on a particular task, dataset, or domain.

questions.question: 96. What is the main purpose of a Vision-Language Model (VLM)?
options: To understand information from both images and language
questions.correctAnswer: To understand information from both images and language
questions.explanation: VLMs combine visual and language information so that the model can understand relationships between images and text.

questions.question: 97. What is the role of the Vision Encoder in a VLM?
options: To extract useful features from images
questions.correctAnswer: To extract useful features from images
questions.explanation: The Vision Encoder converts an input image into visual feature representations that can be used by the multimodal model.

questions.question: 98. What is the purpose of Vision-Language Alignment?
options: To align visual and textual representations in a common representation space
To train only the language encoder
To convert all images into audio
questions.correctAnswer: To align visual and textual representations in a common representation space
questions.explanation: Vision-language alignment helps the model learn meaningful relationships between visual features and their corresponding textual representations.

questions.question: 99. What is the main purpose of Cross-Modal Attention in a VLM?
options: To allow information from one modality to interact with another modality
questions.correctAnswer: To allow information from one modality to interact with another modality
questions.explanation: Cross-modal attention allows information from one modality, such as vision, to influence the processing of another modality, such as language.

questions.question: 100. What is Contrastive Learning used for in Vision-Language Models?
options: To learn similar representations for matching image-text pairs
To train only an image classifier
questions.correctAnswer: To learn similar representations for matching image-text pairs
questions.explanation: Contrastive learning encourages matching image-text pairs to have similar representations while separating unrelated image-text pairs.

questions.question: 101. What is the main purpose of the CLIP model?
options: To learn the relationship between images and text
questions.correctAnswer: To learn the relationship between images and text
questions.explanation: CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training) is designed to learn joint representations bridging images and natural language text from vast web-scale datasets.

questions.question: 102. What are the two main encoders used in CLIP?
questions.correctAnswer: Image Encoder and Text Encoder
questions.explanation: CLIP consists of two separate encoders: an Image Encoder (such as a ViT or ResNet) and a Text Encoder (a Transformer) that project both modalities into a shared embedding space.

questions.question: 103. What type of learning is used in CLIP to match images with their corresponding text?
questions.correctAnswer: Contrastive learning
questions.explanation: CLIP employs contrastive learning using InfoNCE loss to maximize the cosine similarity of true image-text pairs while minimizing similarity for mismatched pairs in a batch.

questions.question: 104. One of CLIP's important capabilities is:
questions.correctAnswer: Zero-shot classification
questions.explanation: Because CLIP embeds images and text descriptions into the same space, it can classify images among unseen classes zero-shot simply by matching image embeddings to prompt embeddings (e.g., 'a photo of a [label]').

questions.question: 105. What is the purpose of prompt engineering in CLIP?
questions.correctAnswer: Designing suitable text prompts
questions.explanation: Prompt engineering in CLIP involves formulating effective text query templates (e.g., 'a photo of a {category}') to guide the text encoder and maximize classification accuracy.

questions.question: 106. What type of data is mainly used to train CLIP?
questions.correctAnswer: Image-text pairs
questions.explanation: CLIP is trained on 400 million (image, text) pairs collected from the internet, enabling broad semantic grounding across diverse concepts.

questions.question: 107. What is multimodal fusion?
questions.correctAnswer: Combining information from different modalities
questions.explanation: Multimodal fusion refers to integrating information from multiple distinct sensory or data modalities (e.g., vision, language, audio) into unified representations.

questions.question: 108. What is a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) designed to process?
options: Multiple types of information such as text and images
questions.correctAnswer: Multiple types of information such as text and images
questions.explanation: Multimodal Large Language Models (such as LLaVA, GPT-4V, and Gemini) process, reason over, and synthesize multiple input modalities including text, vision, and diagrams.

questions.question: 109. What is the goal of Text-to-Image Generation?
options: Generate an image from a text description
Convert an image into a text file
questions.correctAnswer: Generate an image from a text description
questions.explanation: Text-to-image generation aims to synthesize visually coherent, high-fidelity images that accurately reflect the semantics described in a natural language text prompt.

questions.question: 110. What is a major challenge in multimodal generative models?
options: Reducing the number of image pixels only
Understanding and aligning information from different modalities
questions.correctAnswer: Understanding and aligning information from different modalities
questions.explanation: A foundational challenge in multimodal generative modeling is accurately learning cross-modal alignment—binding fine-grained text concepts to spatial visual elements faithfully without hallucinations.

questions.question: 111. What is the main idea of Agentic AI?
options: AI systems that only classify images
AI systems that only store data
AI systems that can autonomously perform tasks and take actions
AI systems that only generate text
questions.correctAnswer: AI systems that can autonomously perform tasks and take actions
questions.explanation: Agentic AI refers to autonomous AI systems capable of perceiving an environment, formulating plans, making decisions, using tools, and executing actions to achieve specific goals.

questions.question: 112. In Agentic AI, what does the agent interact with to perform actions?
questions.correctAnswer: The environment
questions.explanation: An AI agent operates by sensing its environment (digital tools, APIs, web interfaces, physical sensors) and executing actions that alter the state of that environment.

questions.question: 113. What is the main purpose of planning in Agentic AI?
options: To increase the size of the model
To decide the steps needed to achieve a goal
questions.correctAnswer: To decide the steps needed to achieve a goal
questions.explanation: Planning allows an agent to formulate a coherent trajectory of sub-goals and actions required to accomplish a complex objective systematically.

questions.question: 114. What is task decomposition?
options: Combining unrelated tasks into one task
Breaking a complex task into smaller subtasks
Removing all tasks from an agent
questions.correctAnswer: Breaking a complex task into smaller subtasks
questions.explanation: Task decomposition is the process of breaking down a large, multifaceted problem into smaller, manageable, and logically ordered subtasks.

questions.question: 115. What is the role of an LLM in many Agentic AI systems?
options: It acts as the agent's reasoning or decision-making brain
questions.correctAnswer: It acts as the agent's reasoning or decision-making brain
questions.explanation: In modern agent frameworks, an LLM serves as the central cognitive controller—interpreting observations, reasoning about state, selecting tools, and formulating next steps.

questions.question: 116. What is tool use in Agentic AI?
options: Using external tools to perform specific actions
Increasing the number of model parameters
questions.correctAnswer: Using external tools to perform specific actions
questions.explanation: Tool use (function calling) allows AI agents to interact with external tools such as web search, code interpreters, calculators, and APIs to overcome the static limitations of model weights.

questions.question: 117. What is the purpose of memory in Agentic AI?
options: To store and use relevant information from previous interactions
questions.correctAnswer: To store and use relevant information from previous interactions
questions.explanation: Memory mechanisms (short-term context, working memory, and long-term vector storage) enable agents to recall prior steps, retain user preferences, and maintain continuity across multi-step tasks.

questions.question: 118. What is Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) used for?
options: Retrieving relevant information to help generate an answer
questions.correctAnswer: Retrieving relevant information to help generate an answer
questions.explanation: RAG enhances generative models by fetching relevant context from external knowledge bases or documents to ground the generated response in accurate, up-to-date facts.

questions.question: 119. What is a multi-agent system?
options: A system with multiple GPUs only
A system where multiple agents work together to solve tasks
A system that uses only one agent
questions.correctAnswer: A system where multiple agents work together to solve tasks
questions.explanation: A multi-agent system comprises multiple specialized AI agents that collaborate, divide labor, communicate, and solve complex collective problems together.

questions.question: 120. What is a major challenge of Agentic AI?
options: Safety and reliability of autonomous actions
Reducing the number of text characters
questions.correctAnswer: Safety and reliability of autonomous actions
questions.explanation: Ensuring safety, alignment, robustness against unexpected loops/errors, and reliability of autonomous actions with real-world impact is a primary research and operational challenge in Agentic AI.
